folds.subject: Selection policy
folds.why: It is a distinct policy with its own criteria, constraints, and results.

folds.subject: Re-visit policy
folds.why: It addresses when to recrawl pages and how to balance freshness against age.

folds.subject: Politeness policy
folds.why: It addresses crawler impact on servers and ways to reduce overload.

folds.subject: Parallelization policy
folds.why: It covers coordination and duplicate avoidance in distributed crawling.

folds.subject: Restricting followed links
folds.why: It describes criteria for which resources a crawler should request, including MIME type and spider traps.

folds.subject: Focused crawling
folds.why: It is a distinct approach that prioritizes pages by their similarity to a query.

folds.subject: URL normalization
folds.why: It is a distinct deduplication method with its own definition.

folds.subject: Path-ascending crawling
folds.why: It is a distinct crawling strategy with a reported result for finding isolated resources.

folds.subject: Semantic focused crawler
folds.why: It is a type of focused crawler that uses ontologies to select and categorize pages.

folds.subject: seeds
folds.why: It names the initial URLs in the list of URLs that the crawler visits.

folds.subject: crawl frontier
folds.why: It is a distinct part of the crawling process: the evolving list of URLs to visit.

groups.why: s19 explains the criterion used to compare the strategies reported in s18.

s32 illustrates how fast requests and large downloads can burden servers, the impact stated in s31.
